answer.rationale: p99 latency spike on write path with heavy settlement traffic at daily peak suggests primary is under read load pressure. memory_b5 demonstrates that routing report queries to read replicas successfully reduced primary load and recovered latency the same day. This approach: (1) does not require rollback (compliance constraint satisfied), (2) preserves the security patch, (3) targets the symptom (write path latency) by offloading competing read traffic, (4) is reversible if ineffective, and (5) is the only intervention that both respects the no-rollback constraint and addresses load-driven latency. Starting as small_guarded_test on non-critical read queries allows validation of the lever before broad application. Rollback is ruled out by compliance. Regional failover and add_capacity require longer coordination. Circuit breaker protects downstream but does not reduce primary latency under legitimate load.
